This example satisfies (n,p)=1. Q3(μ3)=Q3(√−3) cannot contain √3: that would also put the unramified quadratic √−1 in this ramified quadratic field. The generic SL2 example at p=2 similarly requires √2. Use coefficients containing π and a chosen √p, match the half twist, and put the q-Frobenius statement over k=Fq. The body already requires this extension. The journal introduction, PDF pp.4–5,7, retains the inconsistent smaller field; journal §4, p.1040, requires √p. Confirmed. Item /31 reproduces the commutator-plus-center definition and the affine-simple-root quotient simultaneously (v2 p.37; also journal p.1041). For GL2 over F2, diag(1+y,1) is in I(1), has zero affine-root coordinates, but its determinant 1+y survives modulo squares. Determinants of commutators are 1 and those of scalar central elements are squares. Squaring in F2[[y]] has no odd-degree terms; the obstruction also descends to PGL2 and persists at arbitrarily high odd degrees. Thus these two definitions cannot supply the claimed quotient. Use HNY's canonical filtration: T(1) and the nonsimple positive affine-root groups, with quotient the simple affine-root groups (published HNY §1.2, pp.250–251). Recheck the isogeny comparison using that filtration. The examples suffice; the finding's sweeping iff classification of all bad primes is not needed for this verdict.

Confirmed, with a proof-closure qualification. V2 p.44 and item /38 assert degree-zero holonomicity using an affine τ. In the PGL2 quasi-minuscule Sym² case in odd characteristic, a fibre is a normal surface with its vertex removed; removing a codimension-two point does not make this affine. Locally the singularity is A²/{±1}, rationally smooth over characteristic-zero coefficients. The rank-one coefficient extends across the vertex. Its IC costalk produces a nonzero positive holonomic cohomology group: in the family the cone is a nonzero rank-one object on X in holonomic degree 1. For A→B→C with A holonomic and C in degrees ≥0, one obtains H^i(B)=0 for i<0, A↪H⁰(B), and H^i(B)≅H^i(C) for i≥1, not concentration of B. Replace /38(i) with these statements and write out the H⁰ comparison and its relative-overconvergence argument. I do not certify the entire main comparison proof merely from that replacement. The journal repeats this error in Lemma 4.2.7(i), pp.1050–1051.
